The '''2025–26 Eredivisie''', also known as '''VriendenLoterij Eredivisie''' for sponsorship reasons, was the 70th season of [[Eredivisie]], the premier football competition in the [[Netherlands]]. The league games were held between 8 August 2025 and 17 May 2026.<ref>{{#invoke:cite|web|url=https://eredivisie.eu/news/kick-off-eredivisie-eredivisie-season-2025-26/ |publisher=Eredivisie |title=Kick-off Eredivisie Season 2025/26 |date=17 June 2025 |accessdate=30 June 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{#invoke:cite|web|url=https://eredivisie.eu/news/preliminary-fixture-schedule-vriendenloterij-eredivisie-2025-26/ |publisher=Eredivisie |title=Preliminary Fixture Schedule Eredivisie 2025/26 |date=18 June 2025 |accessdate=30 June 2025 }}</ref> Two-time defending champions [[PSV Eindhoven]] clinched their 27th title on 5 April 2026 after [[Feyenoord]]'s 0–0 draw with [[FC Volendam|Volendam]].

On 15 March, [[NAC Breda]] submitted an appeal against their 6–0 loss because [[Go Ahead Eagles]] had included [[Dean James (footballer)|Dean James]], who had forfeited his Dutch nationality after obtaining Indonesian citizenship in order to play [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – AFC third round|World Cup qualifiers]]. This rendered him ineligible to take part in the match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/knvb-rules-on-passportgate-go-ahead-eagles-to-receive-a-decision/bltc4d519a8d72a1d7d|title=KNVB rules on ‘Passportgate’: Go Ahead Eagles to receive a decision &#124; Goal.com Kenya|date=8 April 2026|website=Goal.com}}</ref> The [[Royal Dutch Football Association]] (KNVB) refused to order a replay of the match but confirmed that James was technically ineligible due to issues with his passport. However, the club and the player were not aware at the time that changing his nationality would lead to legal consequences. The association warned that ruling in favour of Breda could open more than 130 matches to legal scrutiny. On 4 May, the Utrecht Court supported the KNVB's decision.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c5yxd113xjyo|title=Eredivisie: Court rules in favour of Dutch FA in eligibility case|date=4 May 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>
